A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe OpenDance, and their supplied text, equations, figures and tables are readable. v1 includes Appendix A.1–A.4, but v2 refers to a metric appendix that its 11-page PDF does not contain. v1 also references an unavailable user study. These gaps limit verification of some evaluation details.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results and ablations in Tables 2–5, plus generated-motion examples and a cross-dataset evaluation in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark, control and ablation results in Tables 2–7, preprocessing analyses in Figure 3, and controlled-generation examples in Figure 5.

M1.justification: v1's residual motion tokenizer and layerwise motion-token prediction are replaced by DDT with separate rotation, trajectory and keypoint codebooks and joint token prediction. v2 also introduces MS-LRM inference and gradient-based foot-sliding refinement. The data pipeline replaces the cited WHAM estimator with the gravity-view estimator and adds Kalman filtering and MotionCritic-based selection.

E1.justification: AIST++ and the renamed OpenDance corpus remain, but v2 adds AMASS to tokenizer pretraining, extending training beyond the dance datasets. Figure 5 adds explicit last-frame keypoint and user-defined straight/circular trajectory scenarios. v1 Appendix A.4's OpenDance-trained-to-AIST++ transfer demonstration is not retained.

E2.justification: In the corresponding OpenDance comparison, Table 3 removes Bailando and adds FineDance. EDGE, MoMask and TM2D remain. Table 2 retains the same AIST++ comparator set; its changed scores do not constitute comparator additions.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes OpenDance processing from 5-second training clips at 10 FPS to 10-second clips at 30 FPS; AIST++ remains at 5 seconds and 30 FPS. Dataset resampling, temporal filtering and trimming procedures also change. New control experiments introduce trajectory/keypoint distance metrics and a subset evaluation. These are reported setting changes, without independently establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds preprocessing-quality diagnostics, inference-control tests, joint-prediction ablations and a refinement comparison (Figure 3; Tables 3–5). The earlier multi-condition and loss ablations correspond to v2 Tables 6–7, with revised results and supervision terms. v1's appendix transfer visualization is replaced by spatial-control examples.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's dataset-score distributions provide descriptive analysis rather than uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes OpenDanceNet's FIDk from 30.09 to 24.82, PFC from 1.003 to 1.140, and BAS from 0.2545 to 0.2513; MoMask's FIDk changes from 16.49 to 44.92. OpenDance benchmark and ablation values are extensively replaced. v2's refinement improves PFC and FIDg but worsens FIDk and BAS relative to its unrefined model. Changed training and data settings prevent treating these as controlled cross-version gains.

T1.justification: The residual-quantization definitions and layerwise objectives in v1 Section 4 are replaced by modality-specific token definitions and a joint masked objective. The contact-loss expression changes, and v2 Equations 8–9 introduce gradient updates for logits and motion embeddings. These revise the mathematical formulation; neither version supplies theorem-based guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The dataset-plus-controllable-generation thesis remains, but v2's abstract and introduction redefine the central algorithmic contribution around disentangled tokenization, joint spatial/motion prediction and iterative physical refinement. v1's explicit claim that its contributions are demonstrated through a user study is removed.

C2.justification: v1 explains modality imbalance as excessive reliance on spatial signals; v2 argues that coarse stylistic signals can dominate difficult spatial constraints. FK supervision changes from harmful and omitted to beneficial auxiliary guidance. v2 adds a MotionCritic distribution-gap qualification, while v1's FID/user-study caution and broader-impact discussion are absent. The principal hand, face and text-encoding limitations remain.

D1.justification: Hardware disclosure changes from a V100 with 16 GB to an RTX 4090 with 24 GB. v2 adds release-scope information about derived representations and planned source-video links. It omits v1's 100-test-sequence count and Appendix A.2's metric-feature/classifier details; this establishes lost documentation, not necessarily a changed sample count or metric implementation.

R1.justification: Much of v2 Section 2 condenses material already present in v1 Section 2 and Appendix A.1. It updates the discussion with works such as SoulDance, DanceEditor and FreeDance, and adds references supporting the new data and method components. The broad positioning around richly annotated dance data and flexible multimodal control remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Detailed related work moves into the main text, method subsections are reorganized around DDT, joint prediction and inference, and the appendix structure disappears. OpenDance5D becomes OpenDanceSet, with additional author and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. Figures 1 and 4 are substantially redrawn; the retained genre chart is merged into Figure 2, while the dancer-distribution panel disappears. New diagnostic plots and control illustrations replace earlier displays, and the experimental tables gain control, joint-prediction and refinement presentations.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for controllability through direct distance measurements and targeted ablations, and adds useful preprocessing diagnostics. However, it loses metric and sample-size documentation, leaves substantial baseline-score changes unexplained, and does not adequately discuss refinement's competing effects on fidelity and beat alignment. These evidential gains and transparency losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
